question: By what means does the speaker claim to have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of the Kaulas.
The speaker claims to be known or to have come to know.
That knowledge is attributed to the grace of the addressee.
The object known is the determination of the Kaula teaching.
inference: It is solely by the grace of the lord of the Kaulas that the speaker has come to know the Kaula determination.
uncertainties: The verb jñāta allows a slight nuance between 'I am known' and 'I have come to know', though context favors the latter.
plain_english: By your grace, O lord of the Kaulas, I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.
